title: Camp 4 close: you've joined the cycle
hookLine: fourteen portions read closely; the cycle keeps turning, and year two finishes it

lines: THE SAME CHAPTERS, THE SAME WEEK.
cards: Somewhere this week, in a synagogue in Buenos Aires, a teenager is practicing a Torah portion for a bar or bat mitzvah. In Tel Aviv, an old man reads the same portion on the bus.
In a kitchen in Ohio, a family argues about it over Friday dinner. In a prison chaplain's office, in a college dorm, in a hospital room: the same few chapters, the same week, all over the world.
For the last seventy-five days, at your own pace, you've been reading those chapters too.

teach.b: Camp four was the text: one portion a week. It began with how the Torah is read: a handwritten scroll, heard, not just read.
Then fourteen portions, one after another, the way Jews read them. Bereshit, the beginning, and two creation accounts. Noach, and a window in the ark.
Lech Lecha: go, and be a blessing. Vayera: shall not the Judge of all the earth do justly? Chayei Sarah: a death portion called life.
Toldot: Rebekah asking why. Vayetze: Jacob leaving town. Vayishlach: too small for all this kindness.
Vayeshev: wanting to settle. Miketz: it ends suddenly, and Joseph washing his face. Vayigash: Judah drew near.
Vayechi: and he lived, and true kindness. Shemot: names, a lamb, holy ground. And Va'era: four cups, and fire in the hail.
That's the parashah, the weekly portion, and it never stops.
The Torah is divided into fifty-four portions, read in an annual cycle, with some weeks doubling up.

On the holiday of Simchat Torah, they read the last lines of Deuteronomy, and then, without a breath, the first lines of Genesis. In the beginning, again. Some congregations follow a three-year cycle instead.
Either way, the circle has no finish line. This camp stopped at Va'era.
The next portion is Bo, and the plagues continue; you'll pick up the thread in year two. But the cycle doesn't wait.
It keeps turning, and you now know how to step into it.

how: Jews read the weekly Torah portion aloud from a scroll on Shabbat morning, with shorter readings on Mondays, Thursdays and Shabbat afternoon; on Simchat Torah the annual cycle ends and immediately begins again with Genesis.

games.q: it's Simchat Torah. the congregation has just read the last words of Deuteronomy. what happens next?
o: everyone goes home; the Torah is finished.
they start Genesis again right away.
they wait a month and begin again.
games.why: they read the opening of Genesis immediately. the circle has no finish line: in the beginning, again.

practice: Let the fourteen portions pass by in your mind: a window, a blessing, a laugh, a ladder, a coat, a cup, wagons, crossed hands, a burning bush, a finger of God. Which one stayed with you? Hold it.

wordCard.voice: Parashah, the weekly Torah portion, read one at a time in a cycle of fifty-four that circles from Bereshit all the way back to Bereshit again.

orig.note: Hebrew: the portion of the week. The weekly Torah reading.

carryVoice: Your line: the cycle keeps turning. Tomorrow, camp five: the depths, and the wisdom underneath. Camp four, complete.
